stories.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
summary: Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure.
In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet.
Mice given the supplement had lower blood pressure, better memory, and improved social interactions compared with mice consuming excess salt alone.

stories.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
summary: Eating blueberries every day could have surprising effects on mood, according to a small study that found greater reductions in depressive symptoms among older adults who consumed the fruit for three months.
Researchers also detected changes in gut microbial enzymes, suggesting a possible gut-brain connection, although the mood benefits were not statistically significant compared with a placebo.

stories.title: Magic mushroom ingredient takes the fight out of aggressive fish
summary: A psychedelic compound found in magic mushrooms appears to have an unexpected effect: calming highly aggressive fish.
Researchers discovered that low doses of psilocybin significantly reduced aggressive attacks in mangrove rivulus fish without disrupting their normal social interactions.
The findings suggest psilocybin may selectively calm escalating aggression rather than simply suppressing all behavior.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising twist in Japan's 7,300-year-old volcanic apocalypse
summary: A catastrophic volcanic eruption 7,300 years ago devastated Japan, but new research reveals that its impact on prehistoric populations was far more complex than previously believed.
While some communities disappeared or declined, others unexpectedly flourished as survivors migrated, adapted, and found new ways to thrive.

stories.title: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief
summary: Researchers have uncovered three brain pathways linked to lasting improvements in people receiving deep brain stimulation for severe, treatment-resistant depression.
They also discovered that patients who failed to improve after two years shared a striking pattern: insufficient stimulation of a crucial brain connection.
The findings suggest that millimeters in electrode placement could make a major difference in treatment outcomes.

stories.title: Two monster black holes could collide in just 100 years
summary: Astronomers have uncovered compelling evidence of two supermassive black holes spiraling toward a potentially spectacular collision at the center of galaxy Mrk 501.
A previously unseen jet of particles revealed the likely presence of a second black hole, with observations suggesting the pair completes an orbit every 121 days.
Depending on their masses, these cosmic giants could merge in as little as 100 years.

stories.title: Scientists discover that male and female skin play by different rules
summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising difference in how male and female skin repairs and renews itself.
By tracking individual skin stem cells in living mice for five months, researchers discovered that female cells work together in a highly coordinated way, while male cells operate more independently.
This synchronization, driven by sex hormones, helps explain why wounds heal faster in female mice, especially during the first few days.

stories.title: Scientists who discovered a third form of magnetism win major physics prize
summary: Physicists have uncovered a hidden third form of magnetism that challenges more than 100 years of established physics.
Called altermagnetism, the discovery could transform future computing and electronics while opening an entirely new frontier in quantum research.

stories.title: Scientists find a youth protein that helps aging brain cells act young again
summary: Scientists have discovered that a protein linked to youth helps protect the brain’s immune cells from age-related decline.
Restoring the protein in older mice improved the cells’ ability to clear debris and reduced signs of inflammation, raising hopes for future treatments targeting brain aging and Alzheimer’s disease.

stories.title: NASA’s SpaceX launch lights up the sky with a giant glowing jellyfish
summary: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket created a dazzling, jellyfish-shaped glow across the eastern United States as sunlight illuminated its exhaust during an early morning launch.

The mission delivered equipment and scientific experiments to the International Space Station, including research that could advance treatments for blindness, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and other diseases.

stories.title: Archaeologists discover 1,200-year-old mummified hairless dog in Peru
summary: Archaeologists have discovered 1,200-year-old remains of Peru’s famous hairless dogs at an ancient Wari Empire burial site, including remarkably preserved mummies and puppies buried alongside humans.
Their unusual teeth, diets, and burial arrangements reveal surprising clues about how ancient Peruvians cared for, bred, and sometimes discarded their dogs.

stories.title: Fast-moving California wildfire burns homes as people are ordered to leave
summary: Fanned by the fierce Santa Ana winds, the Norte Fire is one of 13 burning across the state.

stories.title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%
summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe.
By moving a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team helped bring its powerful instruments into near-perfect alignment.
Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now produces image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, promising exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.
